title: Nvidia Notifies AIC Partners of GPU Price Hike, Shipments Halted
summary: Nvidia has notified all AIC partners of upcoming GPU price increases, effective in August, prompting major graphics card brands to halt shipments and seal warehouses. The RTX 50 series supply will further tighten from late July onward due to rising GDDR7 and GDDR6 memory costs. This price hike will directly affect consumer GPU pricing, making the RTX 50 series and other GeForce cards more expensive. It also signals broader supply chain stress in the graphics memory market, impacting gamers, PC builders, and the entire hardware ecosystem. Memory cost increases are specified as $76 for 8GB, $114 for 12GB, and $152 for 16GB GDDR6 configurations. The RTX 50 SUPER series is also delayed due to high GDDR7 procurement costs.
context: AIC stands for Add-in Card partner, which refers to third-party manufacturers like ASUS, MSI, and Gigabyte that produce Nvidia-based graphics cards. GDDR7 is the latest graphics memory standard succeeding GDDR6, offering higher bandwidth but currently commanding premium prices. Nvidia&\#x27;s Blackwell architecture powers the high-end RTX 50 series, while the GeForce line uses GDDR6 memory.
